name: TWINE
author: strings-agent
description: MEDIUM. Longest common subsequence. Clue is 'A|B|L' where A and B are random strings (length 11-16, alphabet 4-5 letters) and L is the length of their longest common subsequence. Solution: any string of length exactly L that is a subsequence of both A and B (i.e. an LCS). Scorer uses the iterator trick `it=iter(t); all(x in it for x in s)` twice, ~135 chars, and the required length L is what makes it verify-easy / find-hard. Solve: classic O(nm) DP with traceback, ~0.3 ms. Discovery path: the clue has three '|'-separated fields, the last a small number; a demo shows an answer of exactly that length whose letters appear in order in both halves. Gradient: a greedy 'match the next common letter' heuristic gets a decent fraction of instances right, so teams see partial success before writing the DP.
